verses.1: Praise the LORD, for it is good to sing praises to our God, for it is pleasant and beautiful to praise.
verses.2: The LORD builds Jerusalem, and gathers the dispersed of Israel.
verses.3: The one who heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
verses.4: The one who counts the number of the stars and calls them all by name.
verses.5: Great is our LORD, and abundant in power; His understanding is beyond measure.
verses.6: The LORD upholds the humble, but casts the wicked to the ground.
verses.7: Sing praises to the LORD with thanksgiving; play music to our God with the lyre.
verses.8: The one who covers the heavens with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who causes the grass to sprout on the mountains,
verses.9: who gives food to the beasts, and to the young ravens that cry out.
verses.10: He does not delight in the strength of the horse, nor take pleasure in the legs of the man.
verses.11: The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear Him, in those who hope in His steadfast love.
verses.12: Praise Jerusalem, O LORD; extol Your God, O Zion.
verses.13: For He has strengthened the bars of your gates, He has blessed your children within you.
verses.14: He has set your boundary in peace; He satisfies you with the finest of the wheat.
verses.15: He sends forth His command to the earth; His word runs swiftly.
verses.16: He scatters snow like wool, and frost like ashes.
verses.17: He hurls down His hailstones like pieces of lead; who can stand before His cold?
verses.18: He sends His word and melts them; He causes His wind to blow, and the waters flow.
verses.19: He declares His words to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel.
verses.20: He has not done so for every nation, and His judgments they do not know. Praise the LORD!

notes:
Notes
- v. 9: "the young ravens that cry out" renders עַצְּבוֹתָם as "young ravens" based on context and parallelism, while preserving the sense of "those that cry out."
- v. 12: "extol Your God, O Zion" reflects the poetic parallelism between Jerusalem and Zion, with "Zion" personified.
- v. 16: "frost like ashes" is a natural rendering of כְּפוֹר כָּאֵפֶר, where "ash" (אֵפֶר) can also mean "ashen dust" or "powder."
- v. 19: "His statutes and His judgments" distinguishes between חֻקָּיו (His statutes) and מִשְׁפָּטָיו (His judgments), maintaining the nuance in the Hebrew terms.

- v. 19: "His statutes and His judgments" distinguishes between חֻקָּיו (His statutes) and מִשְׁפָּטָיו (His judgments), maintaining the nuance in the Hebrew terms.
